verdict.rationale: Rootly's docs say it offers both public and private status pages and that status pages can serve internal stakeholders as well as external customers, so private or internal pages are a first-party capability. The evidence never describes how access is controlled or whether pages can be scoped to specific customers. missing for 10: documented access-control mechanism (e.g. SSO, password, IP allowlist), customer-specific audience segmentation, employee-only authentication details, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering leader, I can run private or internal status pages with access control for customer-specific or employee-only audiences

citations.quote: Rootly has two types of status pages available: public status pages and private status pages.
Status pages allow you to quickly communicate information about the health of your services and applications to internal stakeholders and external customers.
